presentingComplaint: Severe throbbing headache, blurred vision and breathlessness for 6 hours, with a 1-hour episode of central chest tightness.
history: Known hypertensive for 9 years, self-discontinued amlodipine and telmisartan 6 weeks ago because he 'felt well'. Woke with a severe occipital headache, then developed progressive blurring of vision, two episodes of vomiting and increasing breathlessness that worsens on lying flat. In the last hour he also noticed a band-like central chest tightness, which - together with his risk factors - prompted the ED team to activate the chest-pain pathway and consider acute coronary syndrome and aortic dissection. No limb weakness, no slurred speech, no tearing interscapular pain, no syncope. Urine output has fallen since morning. Ex-smoker (20 pack-years). No recreational drug use, no sympathomimetic ingestion.
examination: Alert but drowsy and mildly confused (GCS 14, disoriented to time). Grossly elevated blood pressure symmetrical in both arms (no inter-arm differential, equal volume peripheral pulses, no radio-femoral delay). Fundoscopy shows bilateral flame haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots and early disc oedema (grade IV retinopathy). Bibasal fine crepitations with raised JVP consistent with acute pulmonary congestion. Heart sounds normal, no murmur, no rub, apex not displaced. Abdomen soft, no pulsatile mass, no bruit. No focal neurological deficit, plantars flexor, neck supple.

labs.troponinT_hs: 38 ng/L then 41 ng/L (minimal rise, non-dynamic - demand ischaemia)

imaging: Chest X-ray: bilateral perihilar alveolar oedema with upper-lobe diversion, normal mediastinal width and normal aortic contour. 12-lead ECG: sinus tachycardia with LV strain pattern (lateral ST depression/T inversion), no acute ST elevation, no dynamic evolution. CT aortogram (done to exclude dissection given chest pain): no intimal flap, normal calibre thoracic and abdominal aorta. Non-contrast CT head: no haemorrhage or established infarct; appearances compatible with posterior white-matter vasogenic oedema (PRES spectrum).
differentialDiagnoses: Acute coronary syndrome (chest tightness with troponin - excluded by non-dynamic troponin and LV-strain ECG without ischaemic evolution)
Aortic dissection (severe hypertension + chest pain - excluded by equal arm pressures and normal CT aortogram)
Acute ischaemic stroke (headache, confusion, visual symptoms - excluded by absent focal deficit and clear CT)
Acute decompensated heart failure as primary process (reframed as hypertension-driven flash pulmonary oedema)
finalDiagnosis: Hypertensive emergency with acute target-organ damage - hypertensive encephalopathy (PRES) plus flash pulmonary oedema and acute kidney injury, precipitated by antihypertensive non-adherence. Chest pain represented demand ischaemia, not a primary coronary or aortic event.
citations: ESC/ESH - Management of Arterial Hypertension (Hypertensive Emergencies) - 2023
stewardship: Not applicable - non-infective diagnosis; no antimicrobial therapy indicated. Management is controlled parenteral BP reduction (IV labetalol or nicardipine, or GTN/nitroprusside where pulmonary oedema predominates), targeting a ~20-25% MAP reduction in the first hour rather than normalisation, in a monitored/HDU setting; avoid abrupt over-correction to prevent watershed cerebral, coronary and renal hypoperfusion.
contraindications: Avoid rapid/complete BP normalisation (risk of cerebral, myocardial and renal ischaemia)
Avoid short-acting sublingual/oral nifedipine (uncontrolled precipitous drop)
Avoid pure beta-blockade in undiagnosed possible dissection until sympathetic/rate control balanced; here dissection excluded
Cautious IV nitrate/diuretic titration given AKI
edgeCases: A non-dynamic minimal troponin rise reflects demand ischaemia from severe afterload, not type-1 MI - do not anticoagulate/cath reflexively
Concurrent chest pain can anchor on ACS or dissection and delay recognition of the primary hypertensive emergency
PRES on imaging is reversible with BP control and should not be mistaken for ischaemic stroke (avoid thrombolysis)
Screen for secondary causes (renovascular disease, phaeochromocytoma) once stabilised, especially in abrupt severe hypertension
expectedMaiK: Markedly elevated BP (232/134) with simultaneous multi-organ target damage - hypertensive/PRES encephalopathy (headache, confusion, grade IV retinopathy, posterior white-matter oedema), flash pulmonary oedema and acute kidney injury - following antihypertensive non-adherence, with chest pain explained by demand ischaemia after ACS and dissection are actively excluded.
